features.feature_value: Used aggressiveness, fear-inducing content, and personal targeting/name-calling as the main criteria.
features.evidence_span: based off of if the posts were aggressive, fear creating, or personally targeting/name trashing
features.rationale: The participant explicitly lists aggression/fear and personal attacks as the basis for their decisions.

features.feature_value: Expected content of substance; if it was just cursing/name-calling it reduced influence/acceptance.
features.evidence_span: provided anything of substance instead of just cursing,name calling
features.rationale: They contrast substantive points versus mere insults/cursing.

features.feature_value: Physical violence was a hard stop; otherwise they kept the post.
features.evidence_span: as long as no one was calling for physical violence then I let it roll. Physical violence was a deal breaker.
features.rationale: They state a clear threshold: physical violence determines removal/decision.

features.feature_value: They would keep if the point was made without personal attacks/foul language; foul language mattered mainly because it lacked merit in debate.
features.evidence_span: making a point without personal attacks or foul language
features.rationale: Their keep/remove rationale depends on personal attacks and how the argument is framed, even while noting they’re not personally bothered by foul language.

features.feature_value: They support free speech but question why the post includes excessive foulness.
features.evidence_span: I believe in freedom of speech but why put in all the foulness.
features.rationale: They express a stance that combines permissiveness with discomfort at profanity.

features.feature_value: Preferred issues that could support meaningful debate; disliked low-signal partisan dunking (e.g., 'Biden sucks/Trump sucks') and preferred clear, aligned topics.
features.evidence_span: Not something like general like Biden sucked, no Trump sucks, that doesn't seem to be a discussion that really matters now.
features.rationale: They describe what kinds of political statements count as a “real issue worthy of arguing over.”

features.feature_value: Chose posts that felt most oppositional to each other.
features.evidence_span: picking the ones that felt most oppositional to each other
features.rationale: Their strategy is about comparing/choosing based on oppositional contrast between paired items.

features.feature_value: Removed/was influenced by posts that seemed too extreme or spread false claims; also considered attacks against their stance.
features.evidence_span: too extreme or like it was spreading false claims
features.rationale: They name extremeness and misinformation as drivers of their judgment.
